title: I Let the Bocce-Court Clock Catch the Duo Who Booked a Ghost Slot

parts.text: I booked court one at 5:12 p.m. and duo Harlow still had a ghost name on my pallino hour. The sign said: BOOK THE COURT. FORTY-FIVE MINUTES. NO GHOST SLOTS. I was fifty-two, park player, holding a permit. Harlow shrugged. "Duos are the gravel." I photographed the sign, the permit, and the ghost. Then I asked for the court log. At 5:18 parks pinged why Harlow's name was on a ghost slot. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Parks can see Harlow's ghost name on court one during my pallino hour.

social.video_title: The duo booked a ghost slot on my bocce court — Part 1/2
social.description: Bocce, a forty-five-minute sign, a ghost name. I logged the slot. Would you have asked parks?

parts.text: Harlow called it practice until parks asked for the still. I printed the log, the sign, and the permit. The ghost dropped. Harlow booked real names and told the next duo practice was always about optics. Optics is a word duos use when gravel exists. Clock policy now has a second line: GHOSTS ARE NOT THE COURT. I keep court one. Harlow brown-bags the jokes. The gravel finally looks like a permit, not a rumor. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Ghosts are not the court — Part 2/2
social.description: Court log, dropped ghost, and a second line. Was practice ever my pallino?
